Played through most of a year, starting having lag and weird frame skipping in autumn when the leaves are falling. Seems like a memory leak?

Very cute! I love the basic setup of this game and the art is lovely. I think those are 2 of the most important features for a cozy game. 

However, because it is so new it is currently lacking some depth. I'd like to see major farming upgrades built in. Once the game play matches the aesthetics it'll be unstoppable.

The Game feels not finish. The Story doesn't exist at all. There is not really something to do except pay Tax, build a coop and a barn, update the home, getting married. Relationships don't really exist as an example my husband he even sleeps upstairs in a empty room not downstairs with me in the big double bed.

The game is very fun and very cute! I am fully addicted and I can't stop thinking about it. I really like that people in the game age and die, I feel like that makes this game so unique and enjoyable.

I want to be able to recommend this game, but I don't feel like I can because it doesn't feel finished. There are SO MANY BUGS.  Things that seem really basic like not being able to plant a tree (in a farming sim!), not being able to see adult animals information like feeding or health, quest lines being broken and unable to finish, etc. There are so many bugs that their discord has an entire channel devoted to reporting them, which wouldn't be a big deal except that I paid $20 for (what I thought was) a fully finished game. I know its been developed by only two people and I really commend the work they've done so far and how hard they are working to keep up with this release! And if this had been early access or still in beta testing, I would totally understand. And I really almost said that yes, I would recommend it to others, until I remembered what I paid for it. 

Again, this game is really fun and I will absolutely keep playing it. But it's disappointing to pay for a game only to find out its not finished. I am looking forward to all the things they plan on adding though, and the community is already becoming so fun and welcoming. :)

TLDR: Super fun game, it just feels like it was released way too soon. Not worth the $20 at this point, but maybe in a few updates.

I tried so hard to enjoy this. I played it months ago, got bored, and dropped it for a while. But the reviews were so positive that I gave it another chance and committed to finishing it, but it still left me feeling disappointed. I do love the style of the game. The 2D look is super cute, but that's as far as my praise goes.
The world just has no life. The townsfolk have no personality and add nothing to the story, and I really didn't care about any of them. They only existed to complete quests. That's it. It was also incredibly confusing and annoying that everyone would sell things, and you would only be allowed to buy a finite number. For example, if you want to have a nicely organized farm, you might make crop fields 5x4 so you'd need 20 seeds for each crop. Well too bad because the farmer is only selling 14 seeds, so you have to go around to everyone in town looking for 6 more seeds and wasting your whole day away. And don't even get me started on if you're looking for a particular person, say the blacksmith to fix your pickaxe. If he's not at his forge, good luck, you'll never find him because the map will only show you either your family or people whose quest you've finished.
I was also very disappointed in the whole "you can die from disease!" thing. I never vaccinated my character or took any sort of medicine and didn't get sick ONCE. I was hoping for some typhoid or small pox or something! I never even saw any of the townsfolk get sick! Every single one died of old age. I was so desperate for my character to die in the end so I could get the achievement that I ended up just letting her starve rather than wait for her to die of old age.
Like I said, I really REALLY wanted to like this game, but if you want a life sim game with LIFE, this just wasn't it.

I do not recommend this game at all.  I played it for quite a while working on the farm etc.  Once I began trying to form relationships I realized it is very politicized and extremely progressive.  It broke the immersion and game experience for me. I was looking for a game that does not have woke politics and this is not it.  It absolutely ruined the game play for me.

I really wanted to like this game, but after playing for a while I felt like I had to take a step back and stop. I enjoyed myself for the first few seasons, but there were a couple things that I started noticing that hampered my enjoyment.

Gonna start with the things that I genuinely really like about this game because it does have a lot going for it. First off, the art style. It's really cute and reminds me of Paper Mario in the best way (which I think might be intentional given how close the two art styles are). Everyone looks great and I enjoy walking around town because it looks amazing. I also really like the level of customization that you have available to you, as one of my favorite things to do in game was run to the tailor and see what stuff I could get to customize my character. I also reaaaaaaaally appreciate things not being gender locked, one of my least favorite things is having things locked because I didn't decide to play a particular gender character, and having everything be the same regardless of my character's gender was something I really appreciated. I also like how the town always feels like its changing, whether that be through characters dying or being born, or travelers coming in for the town fair. That's all I can think of for now but I do think there's a lot more that's good about this game, but now I'm gonna discuss my main issues with the game.

First of all, I do want to clarify that having the possibility of your fellow town members dying is genuinely really cool. That being said, within the first in game week my entire town caught a disease and the vast majority of them died. The first funeral you go to is really impactful, but then it loses almost all meaning once you have one quite literally every day for several weeks (I think I had like, 10+ in a row at LEAST). Also, all of the carpenters died so I couldn't get any buildings for several days which really sucked (There was a replacement carpenter to replace the starting ones but she also died lol). The death thing is really neat but it just happens way too often to feel impactful, diseases are insane and if one pops up say goodbye to literally everyone you know because barely anyone is surviving that unless you intervene (which wasn't a thing to my knowledge when this happened).

Another issue I had is that you don't have many options for how to spend your time each day. After you water all your crops, you're pretty much limited to fishing, talking to NPCs, or going around clicking every interactable item on the map to get more materials. It's fun at first but quickly gets pretty boring (I'm at winter right now). Maybe it's because I tend to play games for really extended periods of time (like several hours at a time) and I got burned out, but I do feel like I'm doing the same exact thing over and over again. Additionally, all the things to do feel really similar to each other, so I feel like all I'm doing is running around the map collecting stuff, going to bed, then repeating. Just feels like busywork, and I know farming sim games are just kinda like that sometimes but this is the only game so far in the genre where I've felt this issue, and I think it's just due to the lack of variety of activities to fill in the time, they all feel really similar to each other.

Also, I think the final thing is that crops feel really unbalanced. I know this is a casual game, but the multi-harvest plants are so much better than anything else that it feels unfair. From my experience, every crop sells for the same amount, but some of them can get harvested multiple times AND give more than one crop every harvest, while some can only be harvested once and give you one crop. Maybe this got changed since I stopped playing but I was looking through the patch notes and I didn't see anything. Just felt pointless to buy 90% of the seeds when there was a very clear best option. The literal only reason I would plant some of these is if I were trying to make a specific recipe which just doesn't feel good to me.

All that being said, I do think this game is fun for the first several hours. I think the primary issue is that the game doesn't feel like it evolves ever. I got married and had kids but it felt like nothing really changed. Everyone takes ages to grow up even when you set the growth speed to fast and I just felt like all I was doing was waiting for everyone to grow older instead of feeling like I'm making progress. I think if you're not going to play this for very long, it's a good time, but I struggled to want to play this game long term.

I was really enjoying this game but the fact you can only water one square at a time, and there are no upgrades to watering or other tools, really brings down the farming aspect of the game and makes me lose interest in playing at all, maybe I will keep playing and just avoid farming all together. I really hope they Add tool upgrades that let you water/hoe multiple squares!

I was intrigued by the premise of having unpredictable things (like deseases) to stir up a regular cozy experience. But in my hours of playing I've had zero... So the gameplay became repetitive and straightforward, with no special catch. 
Game is still fine. I like the artstyle. Being involved with other villagers are a good thing (you don't do every single thing by yourself). But without the main catch it's like every other cozy game existing out there. I wished it would deliver what it promised. I know it's random, and some people have their first desease after the second year of game. But if a game has it's uniqie feature, I as a player don't want to spend 30+ hours of game trying to catch it and never succeding. And yes, everything was turned on in options, it just never appeared. I got tired of the same repetitive grind. Wishing for something intereresting to start, while it never did.

Although it's a cute and cozy game, there are a few major annoying parts that stop me from playing. People are dying like flies, but I guess you can turn this option off in settings. Everyone gets too old way too quickly. The thing that put me off is no matter how big and awesome your upgraded house is, your family stands in the doorway all the time, unless they go to work and school. Otherwise they never sleep, never use furniture, just stand there all night and half of the day. That was it for me.

I loved a lot of this game, it's really cute, and the mechanics are fun, if a little challenging at times. But there is one massive problem I have with it, that has honestly ultimately put me off of it. My daughter grew up, and that was great, but then out of the blue I got a notification in the mail that she was engaged. To her uncle, her other parent's brother. And there was nothing I could do about it, there was no possible way to stop it, or turn it off.

Honestly don't know if I'm just missing something or what but it feels like there's almost nothing to do in the game other than survive and not dying in the game isn't particularly difficult, I went into this game blind and haven't died once, I haven't found any part of the game really challenging or interesting, there isn't even a real story line other than (without spoiling anything) basically just donating stuff, overall quite boring repetitive gameplay and it looks more fun than it really is, at least the artstyles really nice

I actually like this game but after over 60 hours, it is incredibly frustrating and annoying. I love the premise and atmosphere of the game, the look of it is great. I don't even mind that the character personalities are a bit flat, or outbreaks of smallpox (except when there's a change in season and you can't buy seeds cos everyone's dead). I especially love that it doesn't have the ol' "a relative died and left you this" tired trope. 

BUT there are some serious issues. It can be very hard to work out how things work or what machine uses what without internet searches. The calendar doesn't tell you where events are held or the details of them - again, you have to look it up on the net and hope for the best. The story is really short. I was so surprised when what I thought was finishing a step of the story prompted the credits to role (after playing for less than a game year). Missing out on quests because you can't access the person you're meant to hand it in to isn't fun, either. *Some* can be posted to the quest giver but only occassionally. 

Now...the biggest issue this game has is resources. There are no stores with standard items in stock. You have to buy items from individuals. My house is so crowded with 'indoor' work stations I can't build anymore so my farm items are piling up waiting to be processed. I really want to upgrade my house and my barn but I can't. Why? Because you need paint and steel. How do you get steel? You *might* be able to get a steel bar  from the blacksmith. You *might* be able to get it from the carpenter. You *might* be able to get it from the ship that comes in I think once or twice a season? In a full one and a half seasons not one single steel bar has been for sale, and that's checking the blacksmith and carpenter every single day and the ship when it comes in. 

And of course, the same goes for any item you might need. Need cream to cook with to finish a question? Well, if there's no cream for sale you fail the quest. Because even though you can have a whole bunch of dairy animals and milk coming out the wahzoo, you can't make cream. There are so many things you *can't* make, like sugar. The game wants you to have to be part of the community, so there are lots and lots of things you can't make for yourself that you have to buy, which would be fine, except there's no stable shop items, and almost nothing is available in bulk. Which also means getting your cooking score up is almost impossible. The other issue with cooking is that most of the ingredients can only be used in one or two recipes. There are no generic recipes (e.g. any egg, or any fruit, or any fish). Again, very, very frustrating. 

There's no storage management. You can't sort your chests, name them or auto-deposit from your inventory, which is almost unheard of to bring out a game with no inventory management these days.

This is such a hard game to review. If it was still in EA, I would be more lenient and give this a tentative recommend because there would still be known development time to work out various issues. But this game is out on the market as a supposedly finished game- but it's really, really not finished. And that's disappointing because I love the concept of something that's basically Oregon Trail meets Stardew Valley/Harvest Moon.

The Pros: The artwork, usually. I find the 2d-ish handdrawn art to be charming in its own ways that stand out from most Farming Sims on the market; the 3d ones are becoming increasingly similar in designs and bleeding together. But you can also tell where certain shortcuts were taken with items- there's kids' toys like the pumpkin plush and roller duck that are invisible when you try to place them, or things like the tea set and mantle clock being actual 2d paper-type drawings that look very strange when placed at certain angles on the more substantial tables.

Certain events like the meeting of the coven also stood out as welcome surprises in how they played out and what items were available to trade. (I found it hilarious that the person I could potentially curse was the same npc lady my character's husband was dancing rather near to during the bonfire a few nights earlier, allowing me to headcanon it being the temptation of jealous wife shenanigans.)

The Neutral: Events/holidays. Some are a bit generic and don't seem worth the time to attend- like funerals and weddings for npcs that don't seem to grant any special interactions, and funerals in particular have immersion breaking random daily dialogue with the black clad mourners. Other events might have potential to stand out and have nice collectibles/recipes to shoot for buying- but they're all too f*cking short and it makes it d@mn near impossible to actually interact with the event. Most sims will freeze time once you enter an event area so you can get your bearings for what's there, talk to people to see their unique dialogues, and then go to where competitions or similar special activities are taking place and do the things. This game does NOT. And you typically have very tiny windows of just a couple hours to arrive and participate in anything. I missed being able to participate in the spring activities because i was trying to figure out where they were and what I was supposed to be doing or who i was supposed to be talking to. I looked up a guide to try being more efficient in the summer ones, but even then, with how many people are milling about and the difficulties in trying to click on specific people's hitboxes for entering dialogue when they're in such close proximities to one another- I still couldn't get to do the things I wanted. It's not fun to be trying to race the clock in those sorts of settings. 

Speaking of wonky hitboxes and general control issues, The Cons: 

The game likes to freeze up at times, so be sure to manually save before important events or after accomplishing something you're happy with. Or it will register the WASD controls to move your character, but suddenly won't let you do anything else with keyboard such as open the menus or exit the game or cast a fishing line, causing you to have to use task manager to shut down the game. 

Or you're trying to tend crops, but your sprite suddenly freezes in place and you have to click rapidly or hit a bunch of WASD buttons until it suddenly leaps into action again (most commonly seen when watering, especially if your switching directions and your sprite wants to remain facing the other way.) Trying to get that working again kills your steadily ticking time.

All my chickens and geese have disappeared out of my coop TWICE, despite having plenty of food, and only being a couple days old and aging set to slow, and I hadn't just upgraded it to trigger the empty feedbox bug. Also, when I went to the coven meeting and grabbed one of each kind of new goats, i had to trade a couple normal farm animals to make room for them. Unlike when I've butchered them and all went as it was supposed to- the next morning the mundane animals I sold off were glitching out on top of each other in a corner of the barn. They couldn't be interacted with, didn't show as in stock when I went to the ranching farmer's trade menu, and then disappeared a couple days later.

I've also twice had entire sections of crops disappear overnight- not unwatered seeds, not dry crops continuing to be untended, but fully watered crops that were near harvest ready. It's very frustrating to have like 60 squash who were 4 days into growing suddenly go poof without cause. 

House upgrades lead to new layouts that don't make a bit of sense in conjunction with previous ones, and your stuff ending up in an utterly disorganized pile in a random room that takes a bunch of time to redistribute back to the rooms they belong in. I've also lost a couple pieces of furniture after upgrades; no idea where they went.

Despite my character getting married early-ish in the summer to the carpenter, by mid winter there's still no kids being born. Even after going to the witch's meeting at the end of autumn and selecting fertility as the thing I'd like to boost. So if I want to secure my "legacy", looks like it's going to be adoption needed. It seems like a total waste of my coven wish to still not have a pregnancy take place.

I probably shouldn't complain that our village hasn't been ravaged by diseases, but that's one of the advertised mechanics that's supposed to make this sim stand out from others. Diseases are indeed turned on in options, but besides a small outbreak of the cold in mid-spring that only killed one elderly gent, there's not been a hint of the myriad of diseases we're supposed to contend with.

Lastly, while there's the notable coven meeting with its own small cutscenes that are featured in promo material (or the opening ship crash cutscenes), I pushed through nearly a full year in the game but there's otherwise been very sparse special content or cutscenes that pops up. There's really not much in the way of rewards for max befriending pretty much the whole town beyond the occasionally token gifts given. The dialogues are shallow and become repetitive. Besides the crotchety old lady who wants you to insult everyone else, none of the starting npcs particularly stand out from one another, and it only bleeds together more when the generated descendants start replacing them.

I've only gotten about half the achievements, and haven't been able to see how the full family mechanics work due to the game refusing to let my character get pregnant so far. There's more to engage with, supposedly, and I really wanted to like this game and gave it more than ample time to try redeeming itself- but given all the issues I keep running into, I really don't think I want to keep pushing through all the janky sh!t to find the few bright spots.

Edit- I decided to look something up and discovered that there's supposed to be a chain of quests that start on Spring 6 with Mysterious Noises- but that quest never appeared, and nearly a whole year went by without some sort of failsafe popping off to get it to trigger. So that's likely playing a part in why this game feels so sparse in content. And I do NOT feel like starting a new game to see if it'll work as it's supposed to and plodding through all the other bugs to recover the lost progress from my first game. Not happening. This game needs some serious attention to achieve playability and what's advertised.

There are aspects of this game that work okay, but by and large the balance feels really off in a way that's kind of uncomfortable. This game is still in beta right? It feels like it is. With the aging aspect, there's no reason to get to know anyone or feel close to anyone, they're going to die pretty soon (including your character), and you can turn that off, but people are still going to die in your own (idk if this is a bug, since you can turn off both player and general aging, but they will still die). 

On top of that, gifting seems a bit misleading or broken. Characters will have dialogue that says things like 'wouldn't it be nice to work where (X character) works and get Bread wherever you want! Mm' (or something like it). Suggesting that it's that character's favourite food. It's not. It's a tooltip hidden in dialogue: Go to that shop for bread. But because liked gifts are vague and often buried you can go through 10 dialogue / talk options to get to something that *sounds* like a gift that isn't one. Needless to say I gave that character Bread and they were mad at me, lmao. 

There's no sprinkler system, and the watering can doesn't water larger areas as you upgrade (it just holds more water). Be prepared to waste nearly half of your day or more purely on watering if you want to make a decent profit and have access to food. 

It's *hard* to get access to basic building components. There's a limited amount of wood you can get per day, a limited amount of resources, an extremely limited amount of stone (until you get an ultimate tool upgrade). As far as I can tell, without the extremely expensive *ultimate* steel pickaxe, you have to buy basically all your raw building resources re: mining from characters that are only intermittently available (and who will die, and be replaced by others over time). As someone who has had the satisfaction of mining from Spring onwards in every single other game, this just feels really bizarre and limiting, especially since even with making farming and fishing as easy as possible through the Options, it's just a hard grind to ever have enough gold to do what you need to do. 

In terms of the balance specifically feeling off, as an example, I am mostly only catching gold fish now and getting high gold/silver crops in Summer of Year 1 (the endless grind for resources), yet still don't have a Barn or Coop, because I keep sinking money into raw materials like nails for storage options (which are stingy and cost a lot). 

Likewise, cooking to recipes is both time consuming (you can, at least, leave the pot to cook on its own), and extremely resource consuming. Expect to be using more than 4 pieces of meat (which costs more than your basic tools) for example, plus 15 units of other ingredients, for a single meal. As a result, my cooking skill is still on like 1 or 2 and I live off mostly raw and gifted foods. There's no balance to the way the different skills grow, because you'll be so desperate for food and coinage that things like the extraordinarily resource hungry cooking (where even some "basic" meals require fruits from fruit trees that take a long time to grow), and resource hungry crafting, just fall by the wayside. I can sort of see how they've thought a lot about late game rewards re: cosmetics, but I don't know if the team who have created this game have realised how much of an absolute slog it is to even get there in the first place. Every drying rack, preservative maker etc. takes an inordinate amount of labour, grind and gold to acquire, and does not pay itself back investment-wise for a looooong time. In some cases you're better off NEVER getting some of these things, and just buying them outright in trade, which sort of ruins the reason for / joy of crafting - that you can do stuff so much cheaper and easier and faster than buying it outright. 

There's some niggling annoyances re: QOL like targeting not working properly (i.e. I cannot tell you how many times I've clicked on a storage item or sign and walked straight past it because I didn't get exactly in the yellow box in the perfect way). I wish the game had more signposts or the ability to earn more signposts (maybe that exists, I don't know). As for the Pillars (think Community Centre Stardew Valley but different), there should be an ability to see what you've completed/achieved in your main (possibly Family) section so you don't constantly have to go into the particular section (which involves a lengthy time-wasting walk with no resources along the way) just to remember where you're at. The Community Centre achievements had a nice menu-accessible option which would solve a lot of QOL issues on that front in this game. 

The pros: Despite everything it is playable. The art style is nice, and the characters are cute. The grumpy characters are so grumpy you will almost look forward to killing them (or them dying), which is not something I ever thought I'd say. The fact that ships can visit (inc. pirate ships) is cool. Resource gathering can be enjoyable. You don't have to worry about romance at all aside from getting married to make sure you get some of that sweet sweet child labour both before and after you die, and you won't have to worry about remembering anyone's gifts because every character is transient and they won't clearly tell you what they like most of the time anyway (TL;DR I have maxed friendship for multiple characters just by talking to them so often and *never finding out what they like from them or others talking about them* lmao - me: trying to find out their liked gifts, them: actually talking is fine). The gifting mechanic re: characters gifting you is pretty generous. The lighthouse and ocean locations are great, and the sound effects are well sourced. It hasn't crashed for me, though there's been a few visual glitches, none has stopped me from playing the game. 

I have turned off a lot of mechanics in the game to make it more liveable / enjoyable for me personally, I definitely recommend going into the Options of your game, though try it unaltered first to see what you like and don't like. 

I wish this game had been tested a bit more before launch since a lot of this stuff could have been quickly picked up, especially around targeting, QOL, a more generous watering system, the gifting mechanic, and the unbalanced levelling between skills (I've never seen a stingier cooking system in my life. I could make these foods in *real* life using less ingredients. The reality is that you can buy an iron watering can - a later stage tool - or make one (1) dario burger). 

Farm games are my thing, I've been playing them for over a decade, I've picked up almost every indie one I could get my hands on, and have sunk over 1000 hours (each) into the ones I love most. I was determined to give this at least 10 hours of my time to see what it's like, and started wanting to give up around hour 6. I think I'll keep going just to see out all the seasons, but the appeal of getting close to no one while being able to randomly poison or cough on characters to kill them, is just not that fun for me.
There's too many bugs on-going. No new update on game stories. When I though no more bugs, anymore pop out again, it's endless!

I really want to love this game but the ending was such a disappointment I had to write a review. Don't even bother doing the pillars until the devs possibly add more content to some of the story and content of the game.

This game is fun, however I've encountered some bugs or missing features (scarecrows, fished up bottles, certain forageable items not having any use) and NPCs not selling the right things after a generation passes(animal farmers not selling animals,  farmers only selling fruit tree seeds) which makes me not  want to recommend the game *right now*. However if you are okay with potentially encountering some bugs its a very cute game that I've had fun with.

The game is fun at first and I adore the art style (what hooked me to begin with), but it plays incredibly slow and is unfortunately full of minor annoyances. I like the generation idea in concept, but it doesn't seem to have much of an effect on the actual gameplay as the primary objective seems mostly doable within your first character's lifespan.

[list]
[*]Controller support is broken, it's very difficult to manage your farm (water plants, use machines) with a controller because of weird targeting and some menus won't scroll without using a mouse. 
[*]There is no main shop where you can sell all of your goods, or a shipping box. You can trade with every villager, who all have varying but limited currency. The result is annoying and immersion-breaking, making you run around trying to peddle your wares to every unsuspecting villager that you see each day, taking up time and inventory space.
[*]Frustratingly slow to move around, but also requires daily tasks that combine to just be overwhelmingly tedious, such as the need to collect ice everyday to keep iceboxes running and the very long daily walk through the caves to get ore, all the way at the very end. Fast travel helps, but many key locations lack waypoints, such as the caves, your farm, and especially the area with Plum Grove's equivalent to Stardew Valley bundles. You can't even see your progress on these bundles without physically going there, which is quite possibly the furthest area from your house in the game.
[/list]

[h1]Doesn't feel finished. [/h1]
I like this game, I like a lot of the features that it has. The generational concept of the game play is fairly unique and well implemented. 
The world is cute. The ideas are all nice. The design is lovely. The problem is that it doesn't feel fleshed out.

 The NPC's all feel very much the same. They have "traits" but they don't seem to change much except the repetitive dialogue options that they have are a bit different than NPC's with other "traits". The family just sits on the stairs in my house instead of using the furniture or doing anything interesting. When someone dies you get an invitation to their funeral, but there is no indication of how they died and everyone at the funeral just has their regular interactions. It takes away from the community feeling and immersion.

You can only adopt one pet, but the game doesn't tell you that it just won't let you purchase anymore after you buy the first pet.  There are items that are meant to lead to a quest or something but have no purpose as of now because they devs haven't finished them. The mines are pretty boring as they are. 

The crafting takes an incredibly long time (all day long for one brick to cook?) 

If they can flesh this game out and adjust some of the time mechanics, it will be top tier. For now, I played for a couple of seasons of in game time and now things feel samey and I'm growing bored. I hope they can add some more as I think it has a lot of potential. 

I can recommend this game for about 15 hours of playtime, less if you grow bored easily, and more if the things that I listed above don't bother you.

This could be a really great game. I had a lot fun with it. However, the lack of anything to help water the crops is a soul killer. I understand not wanting to add sprinklers because of the time period, but the watering can upgrades could do more than 1 square at a time. The game has magic potions and you talk to ghosts, but you can't water more than 1 crop at a time? After spending half my day watering crops, I didn't want to play anymore.

I really want to like this game as it is right now, but I sadly don't. My feelings are mixed. This game has the potential of being great, but I don't think it's there yet. I really like the basis of it. Stardew Valley vibe meets historical atmosphere. There are many good things about it. It has a historical setting. It's cozy with some odd eerie ties that make it occasionally a little less cozy. The graphics are crisp. You have the ability to control some game variables, making the game easier/harder. 

The deadlines for quests cannot be changed, and they need to have longer deadlines or the power to remove deadlines! This is one of the most frustrating parts of this game so far. I finish quests only to have to chase villagers all over the place to try and finalize the quest, and then I run out of time, "failing" the quest. I'm left with quest items (some of these items are useless) and failed quests.

Farming needs improving, including irrigating crops and crops turning brown after missing one watering without chance of reviving. Crop names and timers should pop up over the crops or be visible in a hideable side tab. There should be a speed travel for the mines and your homestead.

The areas of improvement make me think of Disney Dreamlight Valley in a negative way. It makes it feel unpolished.

It gets boring quite quickly due to very flat characters, slow game play loop and just grind with no real satisfaction.

As a huge fan of SDV and other cozy games, I was set to love this game, too. I did not. I need to pee and eat on occasion (IRL), so when I pull up a menu or put this game in the background, I expect it to stop. It didn't. When my dog needed to to out, the game kept going in spite of my efforts to pause it, and I ended up starving and exhausted with piles of spoiled food. My sister just called me from Mexico and by the time I got back to the game, my character was dead, game over, starved to death while I was on the phone with a loved one. I tried to reload previous saves but they were all in the dead time. 

Put that in the bucket with a fishing minigame that never worked (I never saw my line in the window and eventually had to turn off the game in the settings), NPCs who are not where they are supposed to be (I tried for days to buy another fishing pole but the fisher was never in the store), no really detailed map of the village that clearly tells you where locations are or where NPCs are, glitches where I couldn't stop my character from moving in a certain direction - it is just poorly coded. 

Between the choices they made that exclude people with a life from playing, and the coding errors that made gameplay too challenging, I just can't recommend it.

First off, I love a lot of aspects of this game, but I struggle to see myself finishing a year due to some issues I have with it. Those issue ended up piling up enough that I just wasn't having fun with the game. It kind of just became a chore.

- Firstly, The death mechanic. Literally every day until the middle of my first summer was filled with either a holiday, a funeral or one of the two weddings that I saw. After the second week, most of the characters I had talked to were already dead, lol. This kind of crushed any desire to get to know anyone else going forward, knowing that they just die almost immediately. I made it almost to Fall, and that trend seems to just keep going with maybe a week or two between waves of death. Maybe I'm just unlucky?

- Second, Your characters movement speed is just insanely slow and a lot of the areas are designed to make you need to walk a long way through mostly empty paths (The mine, limbo, etc). I genuinely don't understand this design decision, as it just makes me want to do less in the game. Should i go to the mine? Nah, I really don't want to spend 3 minutes IRL walking one way just to get 2 iron. Should I go to limbo? But those stairs...

- Third, There is no automated watering mechanic. We have mermaids and witches and ghosts, but no irrigation? wtf? 

- Fourth, Can't see NPCs on map. This became an issue due to having so many NPCs dying that I couldn't keep up with who lived where. You can go into the village menu and scroll through all of the villagers, but with everyone being swapped out every few weeks, it is hard to keep up with who is who.

- Fifth, Family members/NPCs are not smart enough to just go get medicine when they are sick. You end up kind of having to babysit them.

- Sixth, NPCs being unreachable for long periods of time. There were multiple times where I took a mission for an NPC, only to have them either gone in the woods, or unreachable in the lighthouse until the mission timed out. Quests for NPCs who are not reachable should at least be put on pause while they are gone.

- Lastly, Friends and marriage. I don't understand how it is possible to do some of the limbo quests like making 20 friends without entirely disabling several of the game mechanics. Virtually my entire village has died twice over. How am I supposed to make friends with someone when they only live for like a month?

Towards the end of my playtime, I ended up adding unlimited speed potions for myself (Only using them for myself, not to make money) and this made the game so much more enjoyable. I wish that they would add a few quality of life things to the game, or just to options. 

Overall, I don't dislike this game, but several of the issues I mentioned just ended up making it kind of unfun for me.

I have not finished this game, but I feel like I've played long enough to give an honest review.  Do I like this game? Yes, somewhat. Do I recommend it? No, not really. Long review incoming as to why. I played 100% of this game on the Steam Deck, so that will likely influence some of this.

First off, a couple things I do appreciate about this game is the manual save (seriously, thank you for this one. I HATE sleep to save!!) It does save automatically at midnight so there is an auto-save backup which is nice. I also like the art style. Unfortunately it does mean that doing certain tasks become more difficult, such as using your processing equipment (soap maker, mills, etc). It is incredibly annoying especially with controller to get the character clicking on the correct spot. You run the risk of eating raw fish and making your character sick. The controls really need some work. They are janky on controller. There is also a bunch of settings you can change so make sure to check that to customize to your playstyle!

I think they have a nice idea with this game.  But it really needs more work in my opinion. I would have to agree with other reviews that it still feels very early access, and is missing a lot of things that could really add some interest to the gameplay. I actually bought this game originally over a year ago, and ended up getting a refund because it felt so bare. I repurchased it again a year later because it looked like that had been continuing updates and I want to like this game, but it still feels like it is missing a lot.

Here is where it all goes downhill for me. It is loaded with bugs and glitches. Eventually it started to get on my nerves. Winter is a stuttering mess. There are weird glitches on the ground all over that I couldn't tell if it was supposed to be ice, or that the ground was clipping. I messed with the settings but it made no difference. It is also the most boring season. They really need to add in a greenhouse (preferably), or at least some crops that will grow during winter. A shed would be great as well. You will need processing equipment, but I personally hate filling my house with that stuff, although there is still some there, and the other half is all over my farm. A shed would really help tidy things up for those of us who prefer that. 

 There is very little variation in your day. It's incredibly repetitive. (Winter being the worst). There is NO irrigation. EVER. Eventually when you have them, your children will help water. However, I have noticed multiple times where they will just wander off and not water at all, even though there is full watering cans in the outdoor chest. I always have to check during some point of the day that they have watered. There is also a potion, but it doesn't come cheap. There should be some sort of drip system unlocked eventually. It's also incredibly grindy. You have to make sure you are continually shaking any and all trees you walk past because you need a lot of wood. The mines are a waste of time. It's a long walk to get down the mining spots, and there is I think 4 or 5 spots where you are just clicking 'A' maybe 3 times to get a couple stone and maybe a gem at the lowest spot. That's it. You can however teleport out.

There are no descriptions on your toolbar. If you want to plant a specific seed you will need to open your inventory and check what it is, and either remember what it looks like or move it to a certain spot so you don't plant the wrong one. The seeds are a whole other thing. You have to make sure you are checking multiple people for seeds EVERYDAY, because usually they are only selling maybe a handful to purchase. That is, if you can afford it. The day to day routine is generally take care of your farming business, shake some trees, forage some bushes, maybe talk to a few people (they are pretty flat personality wise, wah wah), and do some fishing. There just aren't enough different activities to change up your day.

Honestly, I could go on with even more paragraphs about stuff that either needs to be fixed or flat out annoyed me. I know it probably sounds like I hate this game. I don't, I think it has potential, but I am not sure if they have anything else planned. As is, I am not sure it is worth it. The consensus I generally see around on different forums is that it is boring. Given that, if you are really interested then I would wait for a sale.

The farming takes so long there is no time to participate in town events or exploration. There is no irrigation whatsoever, farming never becomes easier via AoE tools, magic, sprinklers, water retaining fertilizer, etc. 

I've heard that the devs addressed this by adding a (prohibitively expensive) potion your can buy that will cause rain the following day, but that no other QoL measures have been implemented because they really wanted to stay true to the colonial time period.  You can tell historical authenticity is hugely important to them because the game allows the player to enter a same-sex, interracial marriage where even a male spouse can be impregnated just like the 1700s used to be.

Aren't they all such cool concept, I definitely feel like I am living my Anne of green gables dream with this game. However, I wish there were more interesting consequences or story to the game. I have no rooms for decorations and maybe upgrading the house might fix this problem but I still think that equipments should have an option to be placed outside as well T-T  

AnD DoNT GeT mE sTarTed oN the Trees...After you cut all of them out of your farm you are left with either shaking all the trees on the island as your option no.1 OR buy them as option no.2 OR plant some fruit trees to be cut down as option no.3 This game asks for hundreds of woods to upgrade and build, but the wood grinding method is so annoying to me. May we please have normal tree saplings in the game, where its sole purpose is for wood farming pleaseeeeee. 

I honestly think that the game is very interesting and doesn't deserve a thumbs down from my review, but maybe with future updates to give the game a little more OOMPH(?) - for players' motivation sake it could get better *0*

When I first came across Echoes of the Plum Grove on a pre-release Facebook ad, it almost seemed too good to be true. It's always been a dream of mine to have a "Cozy" Story of Seasons/Harvest Moon-esque game set in an historical period, and the setting of Echoes screams Early-Modern/Colonial New England. Needless to say I picked this one up the very moment it became available and very quickly fell in love. The game takes what is great about the genre and puts a fresh spin on it in a variety of ways. The Paper-Mario style graphics are beyond charming, the villager's individual personalities really shine at times, and I found myself playing for about 8 hours in my first session. I was ready then and there to post a review along the lines of "BUY THE GAME, RIGHT NOW, NO MATTER THE COST...IT'S WORTH IT!" I am glad I waited. Don't get me wrong, Echoes of the Plum Grove is a great game... but as it is right now, it is difficult for me to rack up hundreds of hours in playtime. I'm a very seasoned veteran of the farming/life sim genre dating back to the original Harvest Moon games on the SNES and Game Boy, so I know very well how repetitive things can get at times. It is almost a feature, not a bug within the genre. You hit a point where you can whiz through the daily tedium with your brain more or less on auto-pilot and coast through to the next major event or season. It hurts me to say this, but it feels as if Echoes of the Plum Grove falls deeper into that tedium than most other modern games like Stardew, Coral Island, Etc. After your first couple of seasons that once vibrant community feels nearly as flat as the character models. The constant outbreaks of disease and death does keep you on your toes but after you've heard the lot of a character's dialogue tree, there is little there to foster a connection worth feeling sadness over. I totally understand that the game is made by a two-person dev team, and the amount they have been able to accomplish is simply astounding. That being said, I think that the game could have used a little more time before being released, as updates are fairly slow to come and still have not brought the game to anywhere near the potential that it showed in the campaign for funding. There is simply not enough depth to warrant playing a character/family for years and years. I truly believe that if the dev team sticks with it and keeps turning out updates, Echoes has a very very good chance to go down as one of the absolute best the genre has to offer, and I see no reason why it can't  take it's place alongside Story of Seasons, Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, and the other cute and fluffy titans in the cozy game pantheon. I have no regrets whatsoever in purchasing the game. That being said, I feel that if you are on the fence about it then wait a little while and see how the next 12 months or so plays out with updates and features added. If you can catch it on sale, then by all means you will get your money's worth. As much as it pains me, because of the above issue I am forced to not recommend Echoes of the Plum Grove as it is today. I have every confidence that this is only temporary and will change my review accordingly when the game reaches it's massive potential. The developers and discord community they have fostered for the game is terrific and I wish them all the success in the world.

I really wanted to like this game, but it feels like it’s only designed for hardcore cozy gamers. I did enjoy how customizable and inclusive the game is, which was a definite plus. Unfortunately, the overall execution just wasn’t there. I often found myself googling how to do basic things because the game either didn’t explain them or explained them poorly. I finally gave up when I tried to marry a character and it required several unclear steps, and I had to restart the process multiple times. With a bit more polish and better guidance, I think this game could be really great. But in its current state, it just doesn’t hit the mark.

This game is certainly promising however I would not recommend the game in it's current state. Whilst it is fun for some time and has many items and craftables, the dialogue gets very stale after just a few hours. It's a great pity because the whole dynasty feature is cool but I can't find myself feeling attached to characters who mutter the same lines over and over again. There are personalities but they often feel samey with just a few outliers. Interestingly to the game's credit, they do influence the quests that specific personality of villager will give you.

I would say my next biggest complaint is likely the mines too or lack of. It is very rudimentary with it just consisting of a few tunnels you wander through. You make your way through to the end of the tunnels to mine some ore or gems then rinse and repeat the next day. It ends up feeling like a chore you only really do because its a decent way to earn some money.Again, there's no procedural generation or anything literally just a few straight paths....

This game simply doesn't feel like a full release which it claims to be. Whilst there is still a lot of fun to be had, I would wait on this one.
